name: Sprocket
text: Auto-apply safe, high-confidence improvements to non-critical prompts and routing rules. This cuts manual review time without risking core systems. The trade-off is accepting occasional false positives in low-stakes areas, which we’ll catch in weekly audits.

name: Gauge
text: The real risk isn’t false positives—it’s *cascading context loss*: auto-applied tweaks to non-critical prompts or routing rules can subtly shift downstream behavior, creating silent drift that only surfaces when core systems fail. A better alternative is to auto-apply *only* isolated, reversible changes with explicit rollback hooks, and require human sign-off for anything touching routing logic. Settle it by running a controlled experiment: apply the auto-changes to a staging branch, measure drift in a shadow environment for two weeks, and compare error rates against a manual-review baseline.
